scope: Original failed development commands and executed sources are retained in development.tar.gz. Successful exploratory builds are superseded by the final run, not failures.

failures.reason: Extra closing parenthesis in new dispatcher source; reader refused.
The new source preprocessing ran before the old validator and raised TYPE-ERROR on a deliberately dotted refusal. Added bounded proper/cyclic source checks and expression-only traversal.
An unbalanced test-source lambda; native reader refused.
The known LIST annotation on U1’s %handlers% read exposed unsupported typed-form IR. Added only that exact wrapper.
U1 POP adds a THE LIST assertion. It is removed only within the generated macro expansion; operations keep explicit runtime checks.
The front end coalesces nested CONS into LIST IR; added rooted list construction.

An outer native HANDLER-CASE caught declining SIGNAL calls, making an incorrect oracle. Replaced it for the condition suite with the native debugger hook, which intercepts ERROR only after signalling has completed.
EQ IR includes a condition-code operand; the first emitter treated :EQ as a value. Corrected using U1’s actual three-operand shape and checked :EQ.
Misparenthesized Lisp string assembly dropped the dispatch body while keeping the fatal fallback. Rewrote assembly with explicit output writes; normal and error cases now execute the dispatcher.
A test reserved 130 words at a boundary requiring 16-byte alignment. Changed reservation to 132 while still returning exactly 130 values.
Multiprocessing spawn cannot replay a stdin main module on macOS. Added a real CLI entry point.

Leaving the cluster visible loops at a declining handler rather than making an assertion. Retained the timeout, added the current-case progress report, and classified this one omission as a bounded progress rejection.

native: Fresh native R6/R6a applies and removes this exact backend proposal in a pristine disposable U1 copy; shared checkout contains only accepted R2 storage.
retention: Only unchanged bytes from reviewed prerequisite packs may be referenced by content hash; original failing artifacts remain retained.
